translationRepairs: During Guangqi Jin was betrothed to Qi Kerang of Yanzhou; he left Yan in lavish wedding gear with hidden weapons for the ceremony.
During Guangqi, Jin formed a marriage alliance with Yanzhou military commissioner Qi Kerang; he left Yun in lavish wedding gear with hidden weapons for the ceremony.
與兗州節度使齊克讓婚 establishes a marriage alliance with Qi Kerang's house, rather than a betrothal to Qi Kerang himself; 自鄆 is Yun, not Yan.
In Guangqi, Jin was to marry Yanzhou military commissioner Qi Kerang; Jin came from Yan in splendid carriage and dress, secretly bearing arms and armor, to attend the wedding.
In Guangqi, Jin formed a marriage alliance with Yanzhou military commissioner Qi Kerang; Jin came from Yun in splendid carriage and dress, secretly bearing arms and armor, to attend the wedding.
The construction records an alliance with Qi Kerang's house, and 鄆 is Yun rather than Yan.
In month 11 Jin's cousin Qi Qiong, prefect of Qi, surrendered his city.
In month 11 Jin's elder cousin Qiong, prefect of Qi, surrendered his prefecture.
齊州 is the place in the office title; 瓊 alone is the recorded personal name, and 從兄 means elder cousin.
Yan fell and Shigu stormed Yanzhou while Jin and Li Chengsi foraged in Feng and Pei; Jin's sons, Kang Huaiying, Xin Tao, and Yan Bao handed the city to Shigu.
Yunzhou fell, and Shigu stormed Yanzhou while Jin and Li Chengsi foraged in Feng and Pei; Jin's sons, Kang Huaiying, Xin Guan, and Yan Bao handed the city to Shigu.
The name is 辛綰, read Xin Guan, not Xin Tao; 鄆州 is Yunzhou, not Yanzhou.
Xing went to look; its bone and eyes were all unlike an ordinary horse; greatly pleased he said: "The affair is done!"
Jin went to look; its bone and eyes were all unlike an ordinary horse; greatly pleased he said: "The affair is done!"
行 is the adverb 'thereupon'; the continuing subject is Zhu Jin (瑾).
He inspected it—bone and eye unlike any common horse—and cried in delight, "The affair is done!"
Jin inspected it—bone and eye unlike any common horse—and cried in delight, "The affair is done!"
The subject remains Zhu Jin from the preceding sentence.
Jin said, "That old crone is not worth a plan!"
Jin said, "That son of an old slave-woman is not worth planning for!"
老婢兒 is an insult aimed at Yang Pu as the son of an old serving woman, not at an old woman herself.
Jin said: "The old woman is not worth planning for!"
Jin said: "The son of an old slave-woman is not worth planning for!"
老婢兒 means the son/child of an old serving woman.
